{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZY9qPA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDATfk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 35, "title": "Separate scanline HDMA scheduling from HBlank and line rendering", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d`, [`SystemBus::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L170) renders the completed line and requests HDMA at the same 1096-master-clock threshold. [`$4212` HBlank status](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L300) uses that threshold too.

The [Issue #31 timing record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/docs/issue-31-validation.md#timing-convention-and-retained-approximations) explicitly identifies the retained H=274 request as earlier than the references’ H=278 transfer point. Issue #33 corrected row-end metadata ordering but [retained this timing limitation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/docs/issue-33-validation.md#implementation-and-retained-approximations). This is the incomplete correction prioritized by the latest assessment, rather than a duplicate of either completed change.

The shared threshold can service payloads and subsequent descriptor/pointer reloads before their intended scanline phase, affecting CPU register observations, live payload sampling and DMA preemption.

## Expected outcome

Implement an independent, source-backed scanline HDMA scheduling phase. HBlank status becoming set and line rendering must no longer automatically request HDMA.

Resolve the event terminology before fixing the numeric contract:

- [Fullsnes, “Timing H/V Events” and “DMA and HDMA”](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), as recorded in Issue #31, places HDMA activity at H=278. In the repository’s current four-master-clocks-per-dot model, H=274 and H=278 correspond to 1096 and 1112 clocks respectively.
- [Anomie’s Register Doc, revision 1157, “DMA AND HDMA → HDMA”](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt) describes startup overhead and the payload/decrement/reload sequence. Distinguish the internal request, service eligibility, startup and actual bus activity; a documented transfer point alone does not prove the request edge.
- Preserve the two-pass ordering established by [Issue #33’s specification evidence](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/docs/issue-33-validation.md#specification-facts-and-ordering-derivation): all eligible channel payloads precede decrement/reload processing, and freshly loaded rows wait for the next scanline event.

The intended bounded correction targets the documented H=278 phase independently of the existing HBlank/render threshold. Record exactly which modeled event represents it. If the references distinguish an earlier request from later transfer activity, implement and test that justified relationship instead of blindly replacing 1096 with 1112 or double-counting startup.

**Evidence limitation:** this planning inspection read repository source and validation records only. The records identify reference versions, hashes and sections, but their ignored reference copies are absent here. The precise request-versus-transfer interpretation remains unresolved and is a mandatory implementation prerequisite, not a verified hardware claim.

Scope is the existing NTSC, non-interlaced scheduler: separate the events, preserve bus-boundary servicing, and verify their ordering. Keep the existing HBlank/render threshold and scanline-0 initialization convention unless direct specification evidence requires a narrowly explained correction.

Non-goals include complete DMA/HDMA startup, alignment and overhead accuracy; CPU revision differences; arbitrary mid-frame enabling; same-channel DMA contention; PAL; interlace/overscan; pixel-fetch rendering; and electrical open-bus accuracy.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant implementation paths are `machine.rs::{tick,bus_tick,events,hdma_events,hdma_reload,transfer}`. CPU accesses call `events` before advancing their clocks, while general DMA checks HDMA between bytes. Tests must therefore distinguish threshold crossing from subsequent servicing and bus reads/writes.

Existing original tests provide useful coverage but do not resolve this phase boundary:

- [`hdma_init_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/crates/snes-core/src/machine/hdma_init_tests.rs#L58) observes payload completion around H=1150.
- [`hdma_reload_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/crates/snes-core/src/machine/hdma_reload_tests.rs#L41) observes reloads around H=1200; its DMA-overlap vector checks byte preservation and aggregate accounting.
- [`hdma_reload.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f86dc701828bf6f7b3b537454f2b75eb5c96a84d/crates/snes-core/tests/hdma_reload.rs#L64) polls through whole HBlanks.

Reproduce with an original direct/indirect table configured before natural initialization. Advance normal CPU/bus clocks through HBlank entry and the separately established HDMA phase, observing `$4212`, destination bytes, `$43x8/9`, `$43xA` and indirect pointers. The baseline couples the request to HBlank entry; corrected behavior must distinguish the phases numerically.

No tests were executed during this read-only planning inspection.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Reconcile the cited timing sections before changing production behavior. Record reference versions/sections and a numeric event table separating HBlank/render, HDMA request or service eligibility, startup assumptions, source sampling, destination commitment and row-end reload. Identify specification facts versus scheduler conventions. Correct unsupported earlier documentation or test contracts rather than preserving them merely because they passed.
- [ ] Implement the separate HDMA event with no duplicate or lost requests when an access crosses a threshold or scanline boundary. Preserve initialization, channel priority, payload-before-reload ordering, held-row decrement, termination effects and programmed HDMAEN behavior.
- [ ] Add original natural-scheduler regressions for direct and indirect HDMA. Do not inject pending/active/transfer/line state or manually position raster counters. Cover immediately before, at and after each established phase, including an access that straddles it. Assert HBlank/render progression separately from payload and metadata progression. Include a visible-line framebuffer sentinel showing that later HDMA work does not retroactively change the completed line.
- [ ] Cover scanline 0, a subsequent visible line, the final supported HDMA line, VBlank exclusion and the following frame. Verify one decrement per event, no premature next-row transfer, and terminating-row effects at the corrected phase.
- [ ] Add different-channel DMA overlap at the new boundary and across multiple scanlines. Assert payload order and count, row-end reload/termination, final DMA address/count, continued raster/APU progress and absence of duplicate or lost bytes. Separate emulator clock-accounting assertions from hardware timing claims.
- [ ] Add at least one original CPU-executed guest in `crates/snes-core/tests/hdma_phase.rs` that numerically distinguishes the old shared phase from the corrected phase. Configure in VBlank; use executed synchronization and a documented timing derivation, not a broad wait beyond both thresholds. Host code supplies the cartridge and observes bounded WRAM/terminal results only. Document original MIT instruction/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the focused phase regression and guest fail against baseline production code and pass with the correction. Record numeric observations and explain any model-relative latency assumptions. Do not use emulator implementation output as the sole hardware oracle.
- [ ] Preserve existing Rust hardware and guest assertions, licensed fixture pins, game inputs, frame counts, gameplay/audio checks and freeze controls. Any changed timing expectation needs a specific source-backed derivation; do not weaken regressions to accommodate the change.
- [ ] Run and record these mandatory pre-merge gates, using README compiler-selection guidance where needed:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test hdma_init
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test hdma_reload
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test hdma_phase
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
git diff --check
```

- [ ] Use only original or provenance-documented, licensed source-built fixtures. Preserve the mandatory Castle and Memory browser regressions. No commercial ROM/firmware acquisition, subjective approval or deployed-site check is required.
- [ ] Update README limitations and add a validation record with actual results, baseline failures, corrected contracts and remaining uncertainties. Limited passes establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

Inventory scopes and statuses remain intact: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo` and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `dsp-voices` remains implemented_unverified; `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. This Issue addresses one HDMA scheduling gap, not whole-category completion or completion of Issue #3.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
